approach.method_basis: The reference is MolDQN, published by Zhou and colleagues, which applies value-based reinforcement learning directly to molecular graphs, with no generative model in between. It starts from a molecule that already has a real score and then runs a short episode of single edits: add or remove an atom, add or remove a bond, change a bond order, always within what valence allows. At each step it draws a bounded set of legal successor molecules and asks a small neural network which one is worth taking, where the network is given fingerprints of the current molecule and the candidate, how many edits are left in the episode, and the best score the episode has seen so far. Selection is epsilon-greedy, so most of the time it takes the network's favourite and occasionally it takes a random legal edit. The reward is not the new molecule's score but the amount by which that score raises the episode's running best, so an edit that makes things worse earns nothing and is still taken as the next state to build from. That is the point of the method: a molecule can be walked downhill deliberately if the network expects a payoff a few edits later. Because there is no discounting and rewards are increments of a running maximum, an episode's total return is exactly the improvement it achieved. The network learns by double Q-learning from a replay buffer of edits that actually received oracle scores: an online network picks the best continuation from the successor state, a lagged copy of that network supplies its value, and the difference between that target and the online prediction drives the update.
approach.novelty: The commitments this root makes go well beyond the method statement. The reward definition is the largest: rewarding the increment to the episode's running best, undiscounted, is an adaptation chosen so that the quantity the agent maximises telescopes into exactly the best-score improvement the benchmark cares about, rather than the original formulation's terminal-property reward. Episodes are deliberately short, six edits, with ten independent lanes interleaved so that each ten-proposal batch contains exactly one pending action per lane and no lane ever influences another mid-batch. Candidate actions are drawn fresh every time, forty at each decision and eight for each replay continuation, and crucially the continuations used to form learning targets are re-sampled at training time rather than stored, so the action set is never allowed to harden into a fixed candidate library. Value predictions for candidates that were not selected stay predictions: only edits the oracle actually scored enter replay, and a rejected action leaves the lane's state and remaining depth untouched. The root uses one Q-head with a declared epsilon schedule falling from 0.4 toward roughly 0.16, explicitly no ensemble and no episode-fixed randomised value function, so that any exploration benefit later observed can be attributed. Each objective restarts weights, target copy, optimizer, replay and archive from nothing, and preparation stores no learned artifact and no molecule pool at all.

observed_bottleneck: This root has no Parent or evaluated MolDQN node. The difficulty is learning useful continuation values from a small task-local transition history, so an edit with little immediate benefit can lead to a better episode outcome. The confirmed graph-walk node n-6a8d103b076c followed accepted lower-scoring states and sometimes later recovered, but those temporal observations do not establish learned lookahead or its causal benefit. The confirmed CMA node n-bd0cbfe35fa3 reduced heldout reconstruction loss yet reconstructed only 6 of 480 heldout canonical molecules exactly. Direct graph edits avoid that decoder prerequisite; this does not establish a Q-learning advantage. Whether Bellman learning can become useful within scarce feedback is untested.
hypothesis: Select fresh molecular graph edits with a single epsilon-greedy continuation-value network, advance persistent finite-horizon episodes through every matched accepted successor, and learn from accepted transitions using undiscounted episode-best improvement rewards and double-Q Bellman backups through a lagged target network.

finding_summary.headline: Graph-edit Q-learning activated in full but scored 0.4067, eighth of thirteen Discovery roots
finding_summary.insights: The campaign now has a clean answer to a question it could not previously separate: correct temporal-credit machinery is not by itself worth a score. Every part of the Bellman construction was audited and held, including the exact double-Q target, the detached lagged network, reward telescoping, and the use of updated weights in subsequent decisions, and the result still lands in the lower half of the roots and below the frozen-latent swarm root that carries no learning at all. Two mechanisms explain that. The learning signal is thin, because four fifths of transitions carry zero reward under a running-best definition, so most gradient comes from the zero mass and the mean continuation term of 0.014 sits at the same scale as the residual error the network still has, which is also why nearly three thousand continuation values came out negative when the true quantity cannot be. And the search collapses: the molecules produced show that exploitation, once it finds a good core, spends its remaining budget swapping single atoms on that core, which is precisely the behaviour a value function would need a long-horizon reason to escape. For method choice this argues that direct graph editing is the right way to stay in makeable chemistry, but that pairing it with a value-learning controller adds machinery whose payoff is not visible at this feedback scale; the effort is better spent on the exploration and diversity side than on the credit-assignment side. Still open: this is a single seed with no parent and no paired comparison, so the ranking is indicative; the 216 recovered-loss links and 123 later episode-best gains after temporary losses are descriptive and do not isolate learned lookahead from ordinary hill-climbing; and whether episode-consistent randomised exploration would change the picture was deliberately left untested here.
finding_summary.results: One screening seed, macro mean 0.406692671573943, eighth among the campaign's thirteen Discovery roots on a spread running 0.2331 to 0.5103. Per objective the means were 0.7536466193285815 on the docking task, 0.6145349727054742 on the decoration-hop task, 0.33218372414937963 on the zaleplon task, 0.19512536527753646 on the median task and 0.13797267640874414 on the sitagliptin task. Every registered observable moved as intended. The graph sampler filled all 1450 acting neighbourhoods with 40 valid novel candidates each and all 20215 replay continuation neighbourhoods with eight, emitting exactly 29 batches of ten unique molecules per objective with zero invalid, duplicate or rejected proposals; an independent re-execution of 17026 distinct edit receipts reproduced every one. The temporal machinery worked: 250 episode starts, 1200 multistep continuations, and 800 accepted transitions that strictly lowered the score yet still advanced their lane, of which 666 went on to be the source of a later edit. Reward telescoping held to a maximum residual of 5.551115123125783e-17 with gamma exactly one. Of 22900 replay targets, 2685 were horizon terminals equal to reward and all 20215 nonterminal continuation terms were nonzero, mean 0.013847408184662015, so the targets genuinely differed from reward-only regression. Learning registered: mean paired Huber loss fell from 6.10635587187527e-05 to 5.3964929417511364e-05 and mean absolute temporal-difference error from 0.004401601105964189 to 0.004148056249060887, decreasing on every objective, with 1242 of 1450 individual steps improving. The learned values then drove behaviour: 1095 exploitation choices against 355 random ones, every neighbourhood showing nonconstant values, and a fixed sixteen-candidate diagnostic probe changing its preferred molecule 30 times over training. The counterweight is the sparsity of signal: 1179 of 1450 accepted transitions carried zero reward, only 271 were positive, and 2880 of the sampled continuations were predicted negative even though a true remaining episode-best gain can never be below zero.

molecular.headline: Drug-like fused aromatic scaffolds inherited from the seeds, decorated with impossible bonds and collapsed onto one core per objective
molecular.overall_character: Because every molecule is one legal edit away from a molecule that was already there, this node's output looks far more like real medicinal chemistry than a decoder's would. Ring closures appear in 99 to 100 percent of emitted molecules and aromatic atoms in 94 to 100 percent; the sets are full of genuine fused heterocycles, indoles, coumarins, xanthines, benzodioxoles and aminopyridines, carrying amides, sulfonamides and basic amines at sensible positions. The two problems are structural rather than cosmetic. First, the edit operators are constrained only by valence and connectivity, so they cheerfully form bonds that no chemist would draw: oxygen-fluorine, oxygen-chlorine and oxygen-bromine hypohalites, nitrogen-sulfur and nitrogen-chlorine bonds on imide nitrogens, NON(O)O chains, peroxides, hemiaminals, and three-membered oxygen rings fused straight onto an arene. Second, the search converges hard: within any objective the twelve highest-scoring molecules are one- and two-atom variants of a single core, several sharing scores to four decimal places, so what reads as optimisation is largely relabelling. Stereochemistry is absent everywhere and no molecule carries a formal charge.

per_task.generated_character: Two families only. One is a methoxy- or ethoxy-substituted fused indole bearing a carbinolamine and an N-linked fluorinated bicycle, repeated with single-atom substitutions across almost the entire best list. The other is the supplied dimethoxyindole carboxamide with one atom changed. Ring closure and aromatic rates are both at or near 1.0, and the halogen rate of 0.86 comes almost entirely from a single inherited aryl fluoride.
liabilities: carbinolamine and aminal centres of the C(O)N type, which are hydrolytically unstable
sulfur attached directly to an amide or ring nitrogen as a bare SH
a bridged bicyclic alkene written across ring-closure pairs that would be anti-Bredt
a cumulated allene fragment surviving in the low-scoring set
missing_features: no pyrazolopyrimidine or comparable fused bicyclic nitrogen core is ever constructed
no nitrile group appears despite it being a common feature of this chemotype
no N,N-dialkyl acetamide is built onto the aryl ring
no stereochemistry on the sp3 carbinolamine centre the scaffold creates
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top eleven molecules occupy a band from 0.317 to 0.332 and differ from each other by a methyl versus ethyl, a hydroxyl versus methoxy, or the position of one substituent, so score is essentially flat across the whole exploited core. The zero-scoring tail is composed entirely of the supplied starting molecules and their immediate first edits, which means the improvement came in one jump and was then elaborated rather than extended.

per_task.generated_character: A single scaffold, elaborated exhaustively: a methoxy-substituted coumarin or benzoxazinone fused to a three-membered oxygen ring, bearing an aminopyridine that in turn carries a second heteroaryl with sulfur and oxygen substituents. Aromatic atoms appear in 100 percent of molecules and rings in 100 percent, and the mean length of 56 characters is stable across the run, which is what a converged edit search looks like.
liabilities: sulfenic acid substituents written as SO and OS directly on an aromatic ring
a three-membered oxygen ring fused across two adjacent aromatic carbons, an arene oxide
an NON(O)O chain built onto a fused heteroaromatic
an O-bromo substituent on a lactone carbon, which is a hypobromite
missing_features: no sulfonamide is ever formed, only lower sulfur oxidation states
no saturated ring is added anywhere on the periphery
no basic amine or other solubilising handle is introduced
no stereochemistry, even where the fused three-membered ring creates defined faces
per_task.score_gradient_reading: All twelve best molecules fall between 0.594 and 0.615, separated only by whether a given position carries SO, OS, O, S, Br or SC, and by whether the fused ring is a five- or six-membered lactone. The worst molecules, at 0.52 to 0.53, are the supplied starting molecules with a single atom changed. The objective evidently rewards the scaffold much more than the decoration, and the search extracted that in the first few batches and then plateaued.

per_task.generated_character: The most convincing output of the run and the longest, averaging 72 SMILES characters. Almost every high scorer is a dichlorophenyl sulfur group on a methylated diazepane or piperazine, connected through a benzylic tertiary amine to a pyridine bearing a fluorophenol and an acetic acid arm. These are recognisable ligand-shaped molecules assembled by editing the supplied sulfonamide reference, with a halogen rate of 0.92.
liabilities: a sulfilimine-oxide written as C=S(=O)(N), which is not a preparable functional group
an aryl hypofluorite O-F substituent standing in for a fluorine
an S-chloro substituent on an aromatic ring
an aminal nitrogen placed alpha to a ring nitrogen in the diamine
missing_features: the inherited sulfonamide is never rebuilt at full oxidation state once degraded
no stereochemistry on either the benzylic or the ring sp3 centre, both of which a real ligand would define
no alternative aromatic core is ever explored beyond the one inherited from the seed
no amide linker is offered as a replacement for the sulfur-nitrogen hinge
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score tracks how much of that assembled pharmacophore survives. The 0.65 to 0.75 band keeps all four pieces, the dichloroaryl sulfur, the cyclic diamine, the basic benzylic amine and the fluorophenol-pyridine; the 0.23 to 0.46 band loses one, usually by swapping a hydroxyl onto the dichloroaryl or replacing fluorine with an O-F. The near-zero tail is small aziridine and bromoalkane fragments produced early before the core was found.

per_task.generated_character: One core and nothing else: an N,N-dimethyl xanthine fused to a benzofuran, carrying an alkoxyphenyl on the ring-fusion nitrogen. Every one of the twelve best molecules is that scaffold with one substituent moved or relabelled, and the aromatic and ring rates are both exactly 1.0. It is inherited almost intact from the strongest supplied starting molecule.
liabilities: an N-chloro imide nitrogen, which is an oxidising and unstable group
a peroxide written into an alkoxy substituent as CCOOC
an ynol ether, an alkyne bonded directly to an aromatic oxygen
an epoxide appended by atom insertion onto a heteroaromatic ring
missing_features: no scaffold departure at all from the inherited xanthine-benzofuran system
no aliphatic or saturated ring is ever introduced into the molecule
no ionisable acid or base handle is added anywhere
no stereochemistry, though several edits create sp3 ring carbons
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best band spans 0.189 to 0.195, a range of six thousandths across twelve molecules, and the two top entries share the same score to six decimal places while differing by an ether position. The worst molecules at 0.106 to 0.117 are edits of the other supplied starting molecules that never reached this core. So the entire gain over the supplied incumbent of 0.168 is a small decoration effect on a scaffold the search was handed rather than found.

per_task.generated_character: The node's weakest objective. Output is a single purinone or pyrazolo-fused bicyclic core carrying two aryl rings, a fluorine on one of them, a hydroxymethyl on the imide nitrogen and a bare sulfur on the ring nitrogen, repeated with tiny variations. Aromatic atoms are present in 94 percent of molecules and rings in 100 percent, so this is a flat, fully unsaturated set.
liabilities: a bare SH substituent on an imide nitrogen, which is a sulfenamide with no stability
N-hydroxymethyl hemiaminal groups on both imide nitrogens
a benzylic hypofluorite written as COF on an aromatic ring
a thiocarboxylic acid formed by substituting sulfur into a carboxyl
missing_features: no trifluoromethyl group is ever assembled, only single fluorine substituents
no saturated fused ring or piperazine-like system is constructed
no primary aliphatic amine beta to a carbonyl
no defined stereochemistry, which for a target defined by one configuration caps the score outright
no polyfluorinated aromatic ring
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Scores are compressed between 0.110 and 0.138, with five of the twelve best sharing 0.115357 exactly while differing only in where the fluorine and hydroxymethyl sit on their respective rings. The zero tail is edits of the supplied starting molecules. There is no readable gradient here at all: the search found one core early, and moving substituents around it changes almost nothing.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Emitted molecules carry oxygen-fluorine, oxygen-chlorine and oxygen-bromine bonds (OF, OCl, OBr substituents), nitrogen-sulfur and nitrogen-chlorine bonds on imide nitrogens, NON(O)O chains, and a sulfilimine-oxide written C=S(=O)(N). Every one of these passed sanitisation, reparsing and an independent structural re-execution.
transferable_gaps.gap: Edit operators form element pairings that valence permits but chemistry forbids
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Legality checks on valence and connectivity are not sufficient to keep a graph editor inside makeable chemistry. The proposal step needs an element-pair and functional-group context filter, so that a heteroatom-heteroatom bond is only formed where such a bond is actually known, applied before a molecule consumes an oracle call.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In every objective the twelve highest-scoring molecules are one- or two-atom variants of a single fused scaffold, with score bands as narrow as six thousandths across all twelve, and five molecules in one set sharing an identical score to six decimal places. Late-run output is indistinguishable from mid-run output apart from substituent position.
transferable_gaps.gap: The search collapses onto one core and then relabels single atoms
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Sampling a local neighbourhood and taking its best member cannot leave a basin once it is in one, no matter how good the value estimate is, because every legal move is one atom wide. A generator needs a scaffold-level move, an explicit novelty or diversity pressure across lanes, or forced restarts from unrelated regions, or it will spend the majority of its budget confirming a structure it already has.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Sulfonamides present in the starting molecules are degraded to sulfinamides and then to sulfilimine-oxide forms, and sulfur substituents appear across the range from thioether to sulfenic acid within a single best list, purely as the by-product of adding and deleting oxygen atoms.
transferable_gaps.gap: Functional-group oxidation state is edited as if it were a free variable
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Treating a functional group as an arbitrary collection of atoms lets the editor wander through oxidation states that are not isolable. Groups should be manipulated as units with a declared set of allowed states, so that an oxygen deletion either produces a real lower oxidation state or is not offered at all.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring-closure rates of 0.99 to 1.00 sit alongside aromatic-atom rates of 0.94 to 1.00, and no emitted molecule introduces a new aliphatic ring: rings that appear are either inherited flat heteroaromatics or accidental three-membered oxygen rings fused onto an arene.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator builds no saturated or three-dimensional structure
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Atom and bond edits on an aromatic template can decorate but cannot saturate, so the whole sp3-rich half of drug-like space is unreachable. Ring-forming operators that close aliphatic rings, and operators that reduce aromatic systems, are needed for a generator to explore three-dimensional shape.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre rate is exactly 0.0 across every emitted molecule, including the many products bearing sp3 ring carbons with four distinct substituents and the benzylic amine centres the operators construct.
transferable_gaps.gap: No stereochemistry is set even where the edits create defined centres
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: An edit vocabulary that changes atoms and bonds but never sets configuration cannot address any property that depends on it, and worse, it silently produces racemic answers to questions whose answer is a single enantiomer. Stereo-setting operators and stereo-aware features are a prerequisite, not a refinement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Inserting a single oxygen produced peroxides such as the CCOOC ether chain, inserting oxygen next to nitrogen produced carbinolamine and hemiaminal centres of the C(O)N type, and inserting carbon next to an aromatic oxygen produced an ynol ether. None of these were rejected.
transferable_gaps.gap: Atom insertion creates unstable linkages as an unnoticed by-product
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Single-atom insertion is the operator most likely to build a group nobody intended, because the atom lands between two existing heteroatoms. A proposal-time substructure blocklist covering peroxides, hemiaminals, strained fused small rings and heteroatom-heteroatom chains would remove most of this class at no cost to reach.

method_name: MolDQN: Bellman-guided de novo graph-edit episodes
method_thesis: Anchor the root in MolDQN's value-based control of molecular edits: learn future action returns from scored transitions and choose subsequent graph modifications with a deep Q-network. [Zhou et al., Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 2.5](https://arxiv.org/html/1810.08678v3) describe finite molecular edit episodes, fingerprint features and double Q-learning. Our adaptation starts short episodes from task-local scored molecules and samples fresh valence-aware atom and bond edits at each state. A compact Q-network takes current and successor fingerprints, remaining episode depth and the episode's best observed score. Use a single Q-function with epsilon-greedy action selection in the root. Evaluate only selected new whole molecules; values assigned to unselected successors are predictions. Advance each trajectory after its matched feedback, even when the new molecule scores worse. For Top-1 alignment, use reward max(previous_episode_best, new_score) minus previous_episode_best and undiscounted finite-horizon backups: accumulated reward equals improvement in that episode's best score. This reward adaptation is our inference, not the paper's original reward. Train immediately from accepted transition replay using double-Q target selection and a lagged target network, with zero continuation value at episode termination. Retain all accepted intermediate molecules in the task incumbent archive. Interleave episodes according to announced batches, and generate further edits to replace invalid or duplicate proposals. Each decision samples an evolving neighborhood; no corpus pool, complete-molecule retrieval or fixed candidate enumeration is involved. No pretrained generator or external labels are required, and every objective starts with clean learning state. The hypothesis is that learned lookahead identifies useful edit sequences, including temporary score losses, quickly enough to raise the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Learning useful continuation values from scarce transitions is unproven; the paper's much larger training regime does not establish this transfer.
